correctness.rationale: For n=bm+r, subtracting the two floors gives m+e with e the indicator of the upper fractional-phase interval, so the gcd reduces exactly to gcd(r-be,T,m+e). In each nonzero residue class, the highest irrational positive-degree coefficient remains irrational after the affine substitution and rational scaling for every fixed modulus and subprogression. Weyl therefore makes m mod c, T mod c and the phase jointly uniform in the required sense. CRT gives H_c(d); combining the two phase branches produces the weight 2(b-c)/b². Only r=0 needs an infinite sieve. Holdridge Theorem 1.3 allows any irrational nonconstant coefficient in degree at least two, and the linear tail quoted in the same introduction allows arbitrary real intercept and irrational slope. Thus it applies to f(bm). For any fixed d and prime cutoff R at least as large as every prime divisor of d, exact valuations at p<=R are tested modulo the product of p^(v_p(d)+1). The limiting product is obtained by Weyl; the discrepancy from the exact gcd event is contained in the checked large-prime tail. This gives 1/(zeta(2)d²), including b=1. The mixture normalizes, and only this class contributes when d>=b. In the rate calculation, summing the arithmetic progression after the Möbius expansion cancels the full zeta(2) term against the untruncated linear term. The two zeta-series tails are O(1/(b²d)), the bounded rounding term is O((1+log(b/d))/(b²d)), and the explicit d>=b tail contributes O(b^-2) in total. These bounds prove both asserted rates in the specified order of limits. Independent exact arithmetic matched 78 finite CRT cases, 306 finite Möbius cases, and 450 tail cases; these are not tests of the infinite tail theorem.
residual_risks: The nonlinear large-prime theorem is imported, not proved by the finite checks. No effective fixed-b density rate or simultaneous-n-and-b limit was shown.

evidence: Holdridge supplies the large-prime estimate for one floor, and the multi-floor coprimality result has a total homogeneous equidistribution condition. Champagne's inspected Theorem 1.1 is a coprimality theorem under its equidistribution hypotheses; Banks–Shparlinski use finite-type assumptions and give a power-saving coprimality count. The split-polynomial record likewise needs totally homogeneous equidistribution.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Here the phase difference is fixed on each n mod b progression, so joint phase equidistribution cannot be assumed. The one-floor large-prime estimate covers the needed input only, not the residue mixture or the transition with b.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Taking the gcd of the separate gcds would yield the common gcd when the underlying pair agrees. Before flooring, two distinct translates of the same irrational monomial have a difference of degree degree-1, so direct matching to x/b requires degree two. For degree two, shifts h±=±1/(4 alpha b) match the pair exactly over the reals; they are not rational shifts if alpha is irrational. The indexed summary does not establish admissibility or the law in this dependent case. Even if admissible, this construction covers only a special quadratic family, not arbitrary f and the TV comparison.
